items.claim_and_conventions:
A group G is poly-torsion-free abelian (PTFA) if it admits a finite subnormal series
1=G_0 ◁ G_1 ◁ ⋯ ◁ G_m=G
in which every quotient G_{j+1}/G_j is torsion-free abelian. The trivial group is PTFA, using the length-zero series. The term “subnormal” means each G_j is normal in G_{j+1}; normality in all of G is not required.

items.claim_and_conventions: Let G be a PTFA group and let QG be its group ring over the rational field. Then QG has no zero divisors and satisfies both the left and right Ore conditions. Consequently QG embeds in a skew field of fractions in which every nonzero element of QG is invertible.

items.claim_and_conventions: Assume countable choice as required by the chosen tubular-neighborhood and peripheral-system data. Let K be a smooth oriented knot with compact exterior E_K, positive meridian mu_K, and preferred longitude lambda_K on the boundary torus. The orientation extends the orientation of E_K across the filling. Thus the filling slope is the preferred zero-linking longitude; the definition asserts no 4-manifold bounded by M(K).

items.claim_and_conventions: Let knots be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented S³ and let I=[0,1]. Let C_sm be their smooth concordance classes, where equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in S³×I. Let C_top be their locally flat topological concordance classes in that product. Let C_ex be their exotic-smooth concordance classes: equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W together with an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of pairs (W,∂W)≅(S³×I,S³×{0,1}) matching the endpoint knots. For a nonzero integer n set R_n=Z[1/|n|]. Let C^{1/n} be the classes under equivalence witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W with boundary the two standard endpoint 3-spheres such that each boundary inclusion induces an isomorphism H_i(S³;R_n)→H_i(W;R_n) for every i. A knot is pseudo-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth 4-manifold homeomorphic to B⁴, with the boundary identified with the standard S³. A knot is Z[1/|n|]-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth 4-manifold whose boundary inclusion is an isomorphism on homology with coefficients R_n. These are sets of equivalence classes; this definition alone asserts no group structure.

items.claim_and_conventions:
Let V=S¹×D² be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core, meridional disk and product longitude. A pattern is a smooth oriented knot P in the interior of V. Its winding number w(P) is its algebraic intersection with an oriented meridional disk, equivalently the coefficient of the core in [P]∈H₁(V;Z). For a smooth oriented knot K in S³, let e_K:V→S³ be a zero-framed tubular embedding carrying the core to K and carrying the meridian and product longitude to the positive meridian and preferred longitude of K. The satellite knot P(K) is e_K(P).

When concordance preservation has been established, the formula [K]↦[P(K)] defines a set map on each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n}. The solid-torus meridian is strong winding number ±1 for P if, after V is embedded as the standard unknotted solid torus and P(U) denotes the resulting closure, that meridian normally generates π₁(S³\P(U)). Normal generation means that the smallest normal subgroup containing the element is the whole group. Strong winding number ±1 is a separate condition from ordinary winding number ±1. No additivity or homomorphism property is part of this definition.

items.claim_and_conventions:
Assume full AC, matching the chosen finite twisted-chain and maximal-abelian-cover conventions. Let K be a smooth oriented knot, M(K) its preferred-longitude zero-framed surgery, W a compact connected oriented smooth 4-manifold with boundary M(K), and π=π₁(W). Put π^(0)=π and π^(j+1)=[π^(j),π^(j)]. A right Zπ-chain complex with coefficients in a left Z[π/π^(j)]-module is formed by tensoring over Zπ with that module.

For n≥0, W is an integral n-solution for K when H₁(M(K);Z)→H₁(W;Z) is an isomorphism, H₂(W;Z) is free of rank 2r for some finite r, and there are classes x₁,…,x_r,y₁,…,y_r in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n)]) whose equivariant intersection pairings satisfy λ_n(x_i,x_j)=0 and λ_n(x_i,y_j)=δ_ij. It is an integral (n+1/2)-solution when, in addition, each x_i is the image of a class x̃_i in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n+1)]) and λ_{n+1}(x̃_i,x̃_j)=0 for all i,j. Here λ_j is the equivariant intersection pairing induced by the orientation of W.

For a commutative ring R with 1≠0, a group G belongs to Strebel's class D(R) if every homomorphism between projective RG-modules is injective whenever its tensor with the trivial G-module R is injective. In this page R is Q or F_p for a prime p. For a countable discrete group G, its group von Neumann algebra N G is the weak-operator closure of CG in the left regular representation on ℓ²(G), with trace τ_G(T)=⟨Tδ_e,δ_e⟩. The von Neumann dimension of a finitely generated projective N G-module represented by a projection E is τ_G(E); for an arbitrary module it is the supremum of the dimensions of its finitely generated projective submodules.

For a compact oriented 4-manifold W with boundary, sign(W) is the inertia difference of the symmetric intersection form on H₂(W;R) modulo its radical (the subspace pairing to zero with every class), equivalently on the image of H₂(W;R)→H₂(W,∂W;R). Given a closed oriented 3-manifold M, a homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→G, a compact oriented 4-manifold W with ∂W=M, and an extension ψ:π₁(W)→G of φ, the L²-signature sign_G^(2)(W,ψ) is the von Neumann signature of the nonsingular part of the N G-coefficient intersection form. When such a W and extension exist, the signature defect is sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is called the rho invariant of (M,φ) only after its independence of the bounding data is established by a separate bordism argument.

items.claim_and_conventions:
Let M be a closed oriented 3-manifold and let Γ be a PTFA group with group ring Λ=ZΓ and skew field of fractions KΓ. Write the involution on Λ induced by g↦g⁻¹ and complex conjugation on coefficients. If H₁(M;KΓ)=0, the coefficient Bockstein map, Poincaré duality and evaluation define the higher-order Blanchfield linking pairing
B_M:TH₁(M;Λ)×TH₁(M;Λ)→KΓ/Λ,
where T denotes the Λ-torsion submodule; the first variable is conjugate-linear and the second is linear under the chosen right-module convention. Nonsingularity means that the adjoint map from TH₁(M;Λ) to its conjugate Λ-dual Hom_Λ(TH₁(M;Λ),KΓ/Λ) is an isomorphism. For Γ=Z with generator t this specializes to the classical pairing over Z[t,t⁻¹] and Q(t)/Z[t,t⁻¹].

For a homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→G and an extension ψ:π₁(W)→G over a compact oriented 4-manifold W with ∂W=M, define the signature defect by ρ(M,φ;W,ψ)=sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is an invariant of (M,φ) only when a separate bordism-independence theorem applies.

items.claim_and_conventions: Let P be an oriented pattern of winding n≠0 and K an oriented knot. If P(U) bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth 4-manifold B with boundary S³ and H_i(S³;R_n)→H_i(B;R_n) is an isomorphism for every i, then for every K the zero surgeries M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly R_n-homology cobordant, with preferred meridian carried to preferred meridian. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly (respectively topologically) homology cobordant through a 4-manifold whose fundamental group is normally generated by the image of the fundamental group of either boundary component. The category and closure hypotheses are separate and cannot be inferred from winding alone.

items.claim_and_conventions:
Let P be a pattern of nonzero winding n. If P(U) is smoothly slice in an R_n-homology 4-ball, then P is weakly injective on C^{1/n}, meaning P(K)=P(U) implies K=U in that category. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then P is weakly injective on C_ex (respectively C_top). In ordinary smooth concordance, if P(U) is smoothly slice in standard B⁴ and P has strong winding number ±1, then P is weakly injective on C_sm provided the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture holds.

For any pattern P and knots K,J with P(K)=P(J) in one of these concordance groups, the connected-sum reduction constructs a pattern R for which R(−K#J) is concordant to U, whose closure R(U)=−P(K)#P(K) is ribbon, and whose winding w(R)=w(P). If P is strong winding ±1, then R is strong winding ±1. This reduction turns injectivity of P into weak injectivity of R; it does not assert that P itself is weakly injective without the closure hypotheses above.

items.claim_and_conventions: Consider the identity pattern I given by the core of the solid torus, the (p,1)-cable pattern for a positive integer p, and the local-knot pattern P_J obtained by tying a fixed knot J into a small arc of the core.
